title: Equivariant projective immersions of normal quasi-projective schemes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $G$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $X$ be a normal separated finite-type quasi-projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; normal means that every local ring is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here quasi-projective means admitting an immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n])$, with the total-degree grading [def-pc-proj]; an immersion factors as a closed immersion into an open subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. An action is a morphism $G\times_k X\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfying the identity and associativity identities. For any action of $G$ on $X$, there exist a nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], a group-scheme homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ [def-sc-general-linear-group], and a $G$-equivariant immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(V)$. Here $\operatorname{GL}(V)(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(V\otimes_k A)$ for a commutative $k$-algebra $A$; $\mathbf P(V)$ is the projective space of lines, given in a basis of $V$ by $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ for the polynomial ring $S=k[z_0,\ldots,z_{\dim V-1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with $\deg z_i=1$ and the projective action induced by $\rho$. Equivariance is the identity $j\circ a=\rho_{\mathbf P}\circ(1_G\times j)$ of morphisms, so holds after every algebra extension, including nonreduced ones. There is no smoothness, integrality, projectivity or faithfulness hypothesis on $X$. For $X=\varnothing$ one may take a one-dimensional trivial representation.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, take $V=k$, the trivial homomorphism, and the unique map to $\mathbf P^0_k$. The empty subscheme is open, hence this is an immersion, and both equivariance composites are the unique map from the empty scheme. Assume henceforth $X\ne\varnothing$. Choose the immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P^n_k$ in the hypothesis and put $A=i^*\mathcal O(1)$. By [def-trf-relatively-very-ample] this is relatively very ample over $k$. Apply the equivalence of [lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample], with exponent $1$, to conclude that $A$ is ample. Its finite-type hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis on $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; its quasi-compact base hypothesis holds for the one-point affine base. Over that base relative ampleness is absolute ampleness by the definition in that cited statement.

Apply [lem-sfb-normal-line-bundle-power-linearization] to $A$, obtaining $m\geq1$ and a linearization of $L=A^{\otimes m}$. The group is smooth, affine, connected and finite type, the field is algebraically closed, and $X$ is normal, separated and finite type, exactly as required; integrality of $X$ is not required. By [lem-sc-ample-positive-tensor-power], $L$ is still ample. By [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base], choose $d\geq1$ and an immersion $u:X\to\mathbf P^r_k$ with $B:=L^{\otimes d}\cong u^*\mathcal O(1)$. The base is affine and the structure morphism is finite type, hence locally finite type. The tensor power of the linearization of $L$ gives a linearization of $B$: tensor its structure isomorphism $d$ times. Its identity and cocycle follow by tensoring the identity and cocycle of $L$. By the identification of $(\operatorname{Proj}k[x_0,\ldots,x_r],\mathcal O(1))$ with the projective bundle of $\mathcal O^{\oplus(r+1)}$ and its canonical twist in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], $u$ exhibits $B$ as relatively very ample over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ in the sense of [def-trf-relatively-very-ample]. Thus $B$ is a linearized relatively very ample line bundle.

source.place: Agent assembly; WANTED Brion 1703.09506v3 Lemma 2.9; Stacks 01VT, lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample; Properties 01PT, lemma-ample-power-ample

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-very-ample-affine-finite-sections] to $B$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Obtain finitely many generating sections $s_0,\ldots,s_N$ whose morphism $j_0:X\to\mathbf P^N_k$ is an immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction] in degree zero to the same linearized $B$. Its hypotheses hold because $X$ is quasi-compact and separated and an invertible module is quasi-coherent. We get a $k[G]$-coaction on $H=\Gamma(X,B)$; after every commutative $k$-algebra extension $R$, its section action satisfies $(g s)(y)=\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}(s(g^{-1}y))$. The base-change comparison and this formula are clauses of the cited statement, so no finite-dimensionality or properness of $H$ or $X$ is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, degree zero; Morphisms Tag 02NP, lemma-very-ample-finite-type-over-affine

proof.text: The Hopf maps of $k[G]$ satisfy the coalgebra identities by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Apply [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subcomodule] to the finite subset $\{s_0,\ldots,s_N\}\subset H$. It yields a finite-dimensional subcomodule $E\subset H$ containing these sections. By [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], $E$ carries a rational representation $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ and its inclusion into $H$ intertwines all algebra-valued actions. Since $X$ is nonempty and the $s_i$ generate an invertible module, at least one $s_i$ is nonzero, so $E\ne0$. Put $V=E^\vee$. For every algebra $R$, define the dual action by $r_R^\vee(g)(\lambda)=\lambda\circ r_R(g^{-1})$. In bases this is inverse transpose, with inverse $r_R^\vee(g^{-1})$, and the equality $r_R(gh)=r_R(g)r_R(h)$ gives the group law after reversing the order twice. These matrices commute with algebra homomorphisms. The finite-dimensional clause of the dictionary therefore gives a group-scheme homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$.

source.place: Remark 4.1, printed pp.83-84; Proposition 4.7, printed p.86; the dual-action formula is the elementary inverse-transpose calculation written in this step.

proof.text: The evaluation $q:E\otimes_k\mathcal O_X\to B$ is surjective because it contains the generating sections $s_i$. The quotient classification [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] gives a morphism $j:X\to\mathbf P(V)$, with the convention that $\mathbf P(V)$ parametrizes lines in $V=E^\vee$, equivalently invertible quotients of $E$. Let $E_0\subset E$ be the span of the $s_i$. In $\mathbf P(V)$ let $U$ be the open where the restriction of the tautological quotient to $E_0$ is surjective. In bases it is the union of the standard opens on which at least one of the $s_i$-coordinates is nonzero. Restricting that quotient to the ordered family $(s_i)$ defines a morphism $p:U\to\mathbf P^N_k$ by the same quotient classification. The image of $j$ lies in $U$, since the $s_i$ generate $B$, and $p\circ j=j_0$ by uniqueness for the quotient $(B,(s_i))$. Apply [lem-zl-immersion-cancellation] to conclude that $j:X\to U$ is an immersion. Its factorization as a closed immersion into an open of $U$ is also a factorization into an open of $\mathbf P(V)$, so $j$ is the desired immersion into $\mathbf P(V)$.

source.place: Tag 07RK, lemma-immersion-permanence (1); Constructions Section 01OA, section-projective-bundle; Tag 01O4, lemma-apply-relative, quotient classification

proof.text: It remains to check equivariance as morphisms. The section formula from [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction], applied to $g$ and $gx$, says $(r_R(g)e)(gx)=\theta_{g,x}(e(x))$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, every $g\in G(R)$, every $x\in X(R)$, and $e\in E_R$. This denotes equality of the pulled-back sheaf maps; the coaction inclusion identifies $r_R$ with the action on sections. Equivalently the evaluation quotient at $gx$ is isomorphic, by $\theta_{g,x}^{-1}$, to $q_x\circ r_R(g)^{-1}$. Acting by $\rho_R(g)$ on a line in $E_R^\vee$ transforms its quotient precisely to $q_x\circ r_R(g)^{-1}$, by the definition of inverse transpose. By the natural quotient bijection of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], the two composites from $G\times_kX$ to $\mathbf P(V)$ therefore agree on every affine test scheme. In particular this equality can be applied to the universal pair on each affine open of $G\times_kX$, giving equality of the morphisms there, hence globally. This proves the asserted identity and all its base changes, including nonreduced ones.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q08-3514f305f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and all 12 cited statements in full. The new node lem-sfb-normal-line-bundle-power-linearization says a positive power of any line bundle on a normal separated finite-type X under a smooth connected affine G over algebraically closed k is linearizable (KKLV/Sumihiro, Brion 1703.09506 Lemma 2.9). It is true, and the extension to non-integral X via finitely many G-stable normal components is correct. Its cocycle direction matches the coaction node. Small cases (trivial G, a point, G_m on A^1, empty X) behave. It is strictly smaller than the item: no ampleness, immersion or representation. My dup search found nothing; the Pic(G) nodes are about the group, borel-quotient-affine-cell is only G/B, and the coaction/Hopf/Plücker nodes assume a given linearization. Steps: (1) i^*O(1) relatively very ample by 01VM, hence ample by 01VU with n=1; f-ample over Spec k is absolute ampleness. (2) Power linearization, 01PT, then 01VS/01VT immersion (no properness needed); tensor power of theta. (3) 02NP sections node; degree-0 coaction with base-change and section-formula clauses, hypotheses quasi-compact, separated and quasi-coherent all met. (4) Hopf laws, finite subcomodule (Milne 4.7) and dictionary give r; inverse transpose gives rho on V=E^vee; E nonzero. (5) Quotient classification gives j to Proj Sym E (lines in E^vee); p∘j=j_0 on the open U; 07RK(1), checked at morphisms.tex L220, needs no hypothesis, so j is an immersion. (6) q_{gx}∘r(g)=theta∘q_x gives j(gx)=rho(g)j(x) on all R-points, hence equality as morphisms. Batch-5: def-trf-relatively-very-ample (01VM), lem-trf-relative-ample-very-ample (01VU) and lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry (01OA) are generic scheme theory filed in sec-trace-formula; very-ample-affine-finite-sections reaches it only through that definition. None is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all are accepted; tool_uses accepted. No SGA; not a re-split item. Two FIXes in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/: (a) B3: new node now cites [def-pc-module-pullback] for p_2^*, a^* (added to stmt_deps). (b) C1: step 2 claimed B relatively very ample without citation; it now cites def-trf-relatively-very-ample and lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry (Proj k[x] = P(O^{r+1})), which is what step 3 needs.; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
